_readme: THE BORE AT THE MOUTH (2026-10-26, Mark: "a rolling wave on the coast"). A 500 m impactor 800 km off the Merrimack (40.5 N 63 W;
a 1 km one there swung the sea side -110 to +130 m and swallowed the eye; Ward & Asphaug's 1950 DA stood at 35 N 70 W), the eye
to sea, 80 m up, from 16:45Z through the arrival at 30x. THE SHELF RUNG (section 6's rung 2) -- a second solver window over the
Gulf of Maine (`solvers`, 1600 x 1150 cells of ~260 m) that carried the train across the Gulf in nonlinear shallow water until its
crests shocked, the Merrimack window's faces reading its level -- WENT WITH STAGE 2 OF ONE WATER ON THE TREE (2026-10-26, WATER_V2.md 14):
no `solvers`, no box; the window's faces take the analytic wave (Ward & Asphaug, Green's law) until stage 3 imposes the cavity in the
tail's own solve, which is where the shelf's steepening returns. Without the shelf the train reaches the window as kilometre-long
gentle rises (2026-10-26). The bank kernel feeds its face to the crest law, the column plane folds where the labels overtake, its whitewater is Belanger's.
